skill.name: multi-agent-brainstorming
skill.description: Simulate a structured peer-review process using multiple specialized agents to validate designs, surface hidden assumptions, and identify failure modes before implementation.
skill.summary: Run a gated multi-agent design review with specialized roles, explicit objections, and a final decision log.
skill.author: sickn33

content.user_title: Review Designs With Specialized AI Agents
content.value_statement: Single-agent designs can hide assumptions, constraints, and failure modes. This skill runs a gated review with specialized agents and records every decision.
actual_capabilities: Assigns distinct designer, skeptic, constraint guardian, user advocate, and arbiter roles.
Runs reviewers sequentially to keep feedback scoped and prevent uncontrolled idea expansion.
Surfaces assumptions, edge cases, usability concerns, and non-functional constraints.
Requires the designer to answer objections and revise the design when needed.
Produces a decision log with alternatives, objections, resolutions, and rationale.
Ends with an explicit approved, revise, or reject disposition.
limitations: The process simulates specialist review and does not replace qualified human experts.
Review quality depends on clear requirements, constraints, and success criteria.
The skill evaluates designs but does not implement or test them.
It depends on a separate standard brainstorming skill for the initial design phase.

use_cases.title: Validate a System Architecture
use_cases.description: Review a proposed architecture for failure modes, operational constraints, user impact, and unresolved assumptions before implementation.

use_cases.title: Challenge a Product Workflow
use_cases.description: Test a workflow against user expectations, confusing states, poor defaults, and stated product requirements.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Technical Decision
use_cases.description: Create a traceable decision log that records alternatives, objections, resolutions, and the final disposition.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Simple Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this design using the multi-agent process: [design]. Confirm the goal, constraints, and success criteria before starting.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs structured feedback on a defined proposal.

prompt_templates.title: Stress-Test an Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this architecture: [architecture]. Focus on reliability, security, scalability, maintainability, cost, and user impact. Record every objection and resolution.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team wants a broad pre-implementation architecture review.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Competing Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these design options: [options]. Use the stated requirements: [requirements]. Challenge assumptions, resolve objections, and produce a justified final disposition.
prompt_templates.scenario: A decision owner must choose among several viable approaches.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Constrained Production Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this production design: [design]. Enforce these limits: [constraints]. Assess failure scenarios, privacy, operations, usability, and cost. Return the decision log and disposition.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced team needs a traceable review under strict constraints.

output_examples.input: Review a password reset flow for a business application.
output: Decision: Use expiring, single-use reset links with generic account responses.
Key objection: The original flow exposed whether an email address had an account.
Resolution: Return the same confirmation message for known and unknown addresses.
Disposition: REVISE until rate limits and audit logging are defined.

output_examples.input: Compare a queue-based worker with synchronous processing for report generation.
output: Decision: Use a queue-based worker for reports exceeding the response-time limit.
Alternative considered: Synchronous processing offers simpler operations for small reports.
Constraint finding: Retry behavior, queue capacity, and user-visible status require definition.
Disposition: APPROVED with documented capacity thresholds.

output_examples.input: Review a mobile checkout redesign with limited engineering capacity.
output: User concern: Error recovery is unclear after payment authorization fails.
Constraint finding: The proposal exceeds the stated delivery capacity.
Resolution: Keep the existing payment integration and simplify error recovery.
Disposition: REVISE the scope before implementation.

best_practices: Provide measurable requirements, constraints, and success criteria before review begins.
Keep each reviewer within its assigned role and address every objection explicitly.
Preserve the decision log with the final design for later implementation and validation.
anti_patterns: Do not start review with an undefined problem or missing constraints.
Do not let reviewers add unrelated features or redesign outside their mandate.
Do not treat simulated consensus as proof that the design works in production.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a reviewed design, resolved objections, a decision log, and an approved, revise, or reject disposition.

faq.question: Does this skill run agents in parallel?
faq.answer: No. It invokes specialized reviewers sequentially so each objection remains scoped and traceable.

faq.question: Which reviewer roles are included?
faq.answer: The process includes a designer, skeptic, constraint guardian, user advocate, and integrator or arbiter.

faq.question: Can this skill implement the approved design?
faq.answer: No. It reviews and refines the design but does not write, deploy, or test the implementation.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the design, goals, requirements, non-functional constraints, known alternatives, and measurable success criteria.

faq.question: Does approval replace expert review or testing?
faq.answer: No. Use qualified experts and environment-specific testing for security, legal, safety, performance, and operational decisions.
